text:
IncidentBot: alert: sustained throughput/latency degradation in eu-central-1 for model-serving. Metrics: p95 token latency > 750ms, tail queueing and increased request timeouts. Severity: P2. Paging Fay (oncall) and SRE rotation.

Fay (oncall): acknowledging. moving to #incidents-triage. first glance: high GPU mem pressure and host-level packet drops. Gabi, can you take profiling/trace? Hector, check infra overlays.

Gabi (sre): grabbing traces now. 10:02-10:08 UTC window shows repeated GC-like stalls in the runtime when handling concurrent streaming sessions; batch sizes spiking to 24 due to long-sequence fanout; KV-cache churn also visible.

Hector (infra): infra dashboard shows network egress errors on eu-cgen-2 cluster around 10:03. I suspect a tandem of router flaps + host OOMs causing retries. Running quick host health check: `infractl host-status --region eu-central-1 --pool cgen-2`

Iris (prod-eng): heads up 1: we deployed a routing optimizer for throughput yesterday which increases batch_fill timeout to 150ms. Might be interacting badly under memory pressure. Suggest short-term: reduce batch_fill and disable the optimizer for eu region.

Fay (oncall): agree. Gonna do two things in parallel: 1) disable optimizer for eu to stop oversizing batches, 2) move traffic for streaming-heavy tenants to eu-standby pool.

Gabi (sre): creating a temporary rule to cap batch_size: `serving.set-config --region eu-central-1 --key max_batch_size --value 12`

Hector (infra): initiating host draining on the three nodes showing packet drops. command: `infractl drain --hosts eu-cgen-2-21,eu-cgen-2-22,eu-cgen-2-23 --reason "network errors"` 

Fay (oncall): routing change to move streaming sessions:
```
routing.modify --region eu-central-1 --match "session_type:streaming" --route eu-standby-1 --priority 50
```
This should reduce fanout on main cluster.

Jules (support): prepping customer message for affected customers in eu-central-1. Draft short note: "We're investigating degraded inference service in EU. You may see higher latency or timeouts for streaming requests. Our team is applying mitigations. We'll update in 15 minutes."

Kara (comms-biz): slightly longer version for status page: "Partial degradation impacting streaming/long-sequence workloads in EU central. Engineers applying routing and capacity mitigations. Some clients may experience slower responses or retries; targeted tenants notified." Add ETA: 30-45 minutes for stabilization.

CommsBot: status-page: set status to Partial Degradation  eu-central-1 serving. Next update in 15m or upon change.

Gabi (sre): after capping batch_size and disabling optimizer, p95 dropped from ~820ms to ~420ms within one minute. However p99 is sticky ~900ms driven by a small set of workflows with >4k token sessions.

Iris (prod-eng): for long sessions, let's route them to longseq-special which has a different KV cache config and more permissive memory limits. Creating route:
```
routing.apply --match "seq_len>3000" --route eu-longseq-special --policy prefer-isolated
```
Be aware this will reduce overall concurrency.

Hector (infra): drained hosts completed at 10:14 UTC and were removed from rotation; replacement autoscale started. New hosts expected in ~70s.

Fay (oncall): noted. Also toggled proxy circuit breaker to avoid head-of-line blocking: `proxyctl set --region eu-central-1 --circuit-breaker 0.6`

Gabi (sre): tracing indicates a correlation between the optimizer config and KV eviction rate. Metrics: kv_evictions increased 3x after optimizer enabled yesterday. Disabling it reduced evictions immediately.

CommsBot: queued targeted emails to Dedicated customers with active deployments in eu-central-1.

Jules (support): sent targeted message to 28 customers at 10:17 UTC. Template used (short):
"Were currently mitigating elevated latency for streaming and long-sequence workloads in EU (eu-central-1). Mitigations applied: routing changes, batch caps, and host draining. Expect improvement within 30-45 minutes. If youre seeing significant production impact please reply and well escalate"

Fay (oncall): p95 now ~310ms, p99 ~540ms. Improved but still tracking a longtail. Handing off to Gabi (oncall-next) in 30m. Gabi, checklist for handoff: keep optimizer disabled region-wide until RCA, keep longseq route active, watch autoscale to ensure new hosts warm properly.

Gabi (sre): taking handoff. I'll watch for residual queueing and start a targeted test hitting longseq-special with synthetic sessions to validate KV configs. Creating test job: `ci-run longseq-load --region eu-central-1 --clients 50 --seq 3500`

Iris (prod-eng): meanwhile Im opening INF-5582 to revert optimizer rollback until we can tune it. Also scheduling a canary test on a small host pool with increased memory headroom.

Hector (infra): new hosts up at 10:20:55 UTC; warm-up logs show model weights loaded and KV warmed. No packet drops reported on new nodes.

CommsBot: status update posted: "Mitigations applied; performance improving. Engineers continuing to monitor and run validation tests. Root cause investigation ongoing (optimizer + memory pressure interaction)."

(10:33) Gabi (sre): synthetic longseq tests show stable p99 under 600ms on longseq-special. Planning to keep routing for long sessions for 24h while we tune optimizer.

(10:45) Fay (oncall): ok to transition to monitoring state. Gabi will own until 11:15 UTC. Fay -> Gabi handoff complete. Notes: keep optimizer disabled for eu region, maintain longseq routing, keep autoscale thresholds slightly lower to avoid aggressive host churn.

Kara (comms-biz): drafting consolidated customer-facing resolution: "Resolved: Elevated latency affecting streaming and long-sequence workloads in EU (eu-central-1) has been mitigated. Mitigations: routing changes to isolate long sessions, temporary cap on batch sizes, host draining and autoscale; disabled a throughput optimizer pending tuning. We will perform follow-up validation and re-enable optimizer after careful testing. Contact support@redwood-inference.com if you see lingering issues."

CommsBot: posted final status update and sent follow-up note to impacted Dedicated customers.

(11:12) Gabi (sre): p95=260ms p99=410ms. Marking incident as mitigated for now; keeping follow-up actions: 1) prod-eng to tune optimizer, 2) infra to monitor autoscale churn, 3) SRE to draft short RCA.

Jules (support): sending sticky follow-up to customers summarizing mitigations and next steps.

Kara (comms-biz): prepping FAQ for customers covering retry guidance, recommended client-side timeouts, and how to contact support for urgent issues.

IncidentBot: incident 1961129999 transitioned to mitigated at 11:15:00 UTC. Postmortem owner: Iris (prod-eng). Please coordinate RCA and customer FAQ.

Fay (oncall): thanks everyone for the quick triage. Gabi, please leave the optimizer disabled until Iris confirms tuning and canary passes. I'll file the oncall handoff note in the runbook. Link: https://ops.redwood/runbooks/throughput-degradation

Iris (prod-eng): will draft RCA and target EOD for first postmortem draft. Assigning INF-5582 to optimizer tuning with owner @Iris.

CommsBot: reminder scheduled: 24h recheck to confirm route rollback plan before re-enabling optimizer.

(11:35) Gabi (sre): closing incident thread. Remaining tasks tracked in INF-5582 and infra ticket INF-5583.

(11:36) Jules (support): adding a note to customer threads for any customers who replied.

(11:50) Kara (comms-biz): final: thanks team  good job on containment and comms.
